findings.summary: Bounded routing needs an event-capacity and terminal-delivery rule that remains nonblocking under the engine lock.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/66/design.md:41–45 sends bounded events and removes the route at a terminal event; :98–100 derives queue capacities from queues×depth without specifying event slots or full/closed handling. The retained #15 router contract (design.md, The router, lines31–37) routes under the engine lock through nonblocking try_send. Current ublk.rs:605–615 ignores try_send failure and removes the waiter for Done. One legitimate depth-one read crossing two remote chunk pieces can generate Piece, Piece, Done before its consumer runs (engine.rs:1889–1900 emits each direct-read Piece; sub_done then emits Done). A request-count bound alone is not an event bound. Converting these channels to bounded queues without a stated mailbox/credit policy can discard Done after route removal, hang the request and exhaust the binding; blocking on capacity while holding the engine lock can deadlock the read/stop path.
findings.fix: Specify a concrete nonblocking bounded mailbox/credit policy in event units, accounting for the maximum pieces and terminal result per admitted request and any retained retry/control events. Reserve capacity before engine admission or retain terminal state separately; never remove a live route before its terminal result is durably owned by the mailbox. State full/closed behavior explicitly (safe binding failure is acceptable, silent event loss is not), preserving memory and local-I/O ownership during stop. Add a paused-consumer depth-one multi-piece read fixture, saturated/closed mailbox and stop race fixtures proving terminal delivery or explicit fail-closed completion without an engine-lock wait.

findings.summary: The frontend batch lifetime contract does not define how unwinding is stopped before pending kernel buffers are destroyed.
findings.evidence: spec.md S5 promises safety on unwind, while design.md:73–84 says batches retain ownership and invokes an existing daemon fail-stop path if draining is impossible, but does not define an armed unwind/drop guard or its destruction order. Current local_read and fast_read_copy in ublk.rs:1293–1341,1638–1694 publish raw-buffer SQEs while building pending Vecs. Pinned libublk0.4.8 io.rs:2231–2233 unwraps submission, uring_async.rs:546–570 eagerly pushes SQEs before returning the future, and UblkUringOpFuture (uring_async.rs:26–90) has no draining Drop. Ordinary future/Vec ownership therefore does not keep a request buffer alive when its task unwinds or is dropped with SQEs outstanding. #85 explicitly adds armed abort-on-unwind protection to UringDevice; that separate device ring does not protect the ublk queue ring, and the current flaminio-io daemon has no existing abort/exit path to invoke here.
findings.fix: Define the queue-local batch ownership mechanism explicitly: prepare lengths/buffers/bookkeeping before the first publication, arm a fail-stop-on-unwind/drop guard before any SQE can be published, and retain it through every completion and ownership-releasing cleanup. Its guard must execute before borrowed buffers/plans/tasks can be destroyed, with partial publication or unprovable drain terminating the process without unwinding those owners. Ordinary cancellation/error must drain before release. This can follow #85’s principle without adding an external protocol or changing the settled thin-signature prototype. Add subprocess/injected-backend fixtures for panic after first publication, partial setup, task cancellation and panic during completion/cleanup; prove fail-stop occurs before a tracked pending backing allocation is released, using an independent backing reference so the test never creates dangling kernel memory.
